item.title: Outcomes aim to boost trade and connectivity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economic leaders have agreed on measures to facilitate cross-border trade, strengthen regional connectivity and harness emerging technologies to promote employment and prosperity. The measures are set out in three documents adopted at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, which concluded in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Thursday. All three outcome documents support efforts to realize the APEC Putrajaya Vision 2040 goal of building an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community. The APEC Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework (2027-2030) aims to promote cross-border trade and investment, as advances in digital technology continue to profoundly reshape international trade and the way it is managed. The framework promotes policy exchange and the use of digital technologies to streamline trade procedures. To reduce clearance costs and time, the framework encourages economies to make electronic trade administration forms available to the public and to recognize electronically submitted forms as legally equivalent to paper versions. It also sets out plans for cooperation to facilitate cross-border data flows and strengthen business and consumer trust in digital transactions. The framework acknowledges the importance of data protection and privacy. The APEC Connectivity Blueprint addresses the movement of goods, services, capital and people across the region. Building on cooperation under the 2015-25 blueprint, it encourages economies to advance physical, institutional and people-to-people connectivity toward a seamlessly and comprehensively connected and integrated Asia-Pacific region. The blueprint encourages economies to develop, maintain and upgrade quality infrastructure. To reduce institutional barriers to trade and investment, it also promotes customs modernization, cooperation on technical standards and good regulatory practices. The blueprint also encourages efforts to address supply chain chokepoints, enhance resilience and minimize disruptions. To strengthen people-to-people connectivity, it promotes business mobility through the APEC Business Travel Card, alongside exchanges in education and vocational training. The meeting also endorsed the APEC Statement on Harnessing Digital and Emerging Technologies for Employment and Prosperity in the Asia-Pacific Region. The statement calls for using digital and emerging technologies to promote high-quality and full employment and accelerate the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises. It emphasizes capacity building, wider digital access, and digital literacy and skills training to help workers and businesses adapt. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Intl network launched to streamline silk standards
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
The world's first international science and technology organization in the textile sector to be headquartered in China was formally established in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, on Friday, marking a new step in China-led international efforts to promote cooperation on silk industry standards, technology and development. With more than 100 member organizations from over 20 countries and regions, the agenda of the China-initiated International Network for Silk covers the entire silk value chain, including sericulture resource development, production and processing, and trade and investment, according to official information released during the founding ceremony. "Under the framework of the network, we should build a public service platform to share information, match supply and demand, enhance exchanges and advance cooperation, as well as to promote practical collaboration across the silk value chain," Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing said on Friday during the ceremony. Efforts should be made to strengthen mutual recognition of standards, align rules and promote industrial coordination in the silk sector, while building an integrated innovation ecosystem, he said. Zhang also called for greater cultural exchanges, including cross-border showcases of silk-making techniques, visits by inheritors of intangible cultural heritage and joint projects by designers from different countries. China's position as a major player in the global silk industry provides an important foundation for the initiative. The country accounted for about 75 percent of global cocoon production and more than 60 percent of raw silk exports by the end of 2025, according to the Ministry of Commerce.

item.title: Closer cooperation with Malaysia to bring more benefits
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
President Xi Jinping called on China and Malaysia to deepen strategic coordination and jointly advance global governance reform to safeguard the common interests of developing countries during a meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Friday. Xi recalled that he and Anwar reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future in April last year. China is ready to work with Malaysia to uphold the original aspiration of establishing diplomatic ties, foster greater momentum for cooperation and further advance the building of a China-Malaysia community with a shared future to bring greater benefits to both peoples, Xi said. He emphasized that bilateral relations enjoy a solid political foundation, distinct strengths in cooperation and broad prospects for development. China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said. The two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand agricultural trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas, he added. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks, and safeguard common interests. Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the one-China policy. He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence.

item.title: Stronger solidarity, coordination with Thailand sought
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
President Xi Jinping called on China and Thailand to cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation to jointly build a regional hub for technological innovation and industrial cooperation. He made the remarks during a meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, adding that China and Thailand should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination. China firmly supports Thailand in achieving national stability and development, Xi said. He expressed readiness to work with Thailand to advance the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future and contribute more to regional peace, stability and prosperity. Xi called for closer exchanges between governments, parties and legislative bodies, greater sharing of governance experience, and efforts to safeguard their common strategic interests. He called on both sides to better align their strategies, make full use of cooperation mechanisms and strengthen cooperation in established areas. He also urged stronger cooperation in culture, education and tourism. Both sides should intensify efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud, he said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. Anutin said Thailand firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade and investment. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes, protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, and welcome more Chinese tourists, he added.

item.title: Stronger mutual trust with Australia emphasized
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or fundamental conflicts of interests. He made the remarks when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, where they attended the recently concluded 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting. Noting that China-Australia relations are stable at present, Xi said that both countries should take the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year as an opportunity to promote greater development of bilateral ties in the spirit of equality, seek common ground while reserving differences, and pursue mutually beneficial cooperation. Amid a complex international landscape, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, view each other rationally, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the direction of friendship and cooperation, he said. Xi called for further advancing cooperation in traditional sectors, including agriculture, energy and minerals, and enhancing partnership in emerging fields such as the green economy, new energy, digital industry, artificial intelligence and climate response, in order to jointly share opportunities and pursue common development. Economic and trade cooperation remains the ballast of China-Australia relations. China has been Australia's largest trading partner, source of imports and export market for 17 consecutive years. The two countries have had a long and highly productive partnership in iron ore and steel. According to the General Administration of Customs, bilateral trade reached approximately $206.58 billion in 2025, with China's exports to Australia worth $76.33 billion, a year-on-year increase of 7.9 percent. In the first eight months of 2026, the total trade in goods between China and Australia was worth $176.9 billion, up 34.8 percent year-on-year. While emphasizing the importance of promoting the countries' friendship by expanding cultural and people-to-people exchanges, Xi said that China and Australia should strengthen multilateral coordination to address global challenges. The two countries should advance the building of the Asia-Pacific community, and jointly safeguard the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order underpinned by international law, he said. Albanese said the improvement and development of Australia-China relations serve the interests of both sides, and have brought tangible benefits to the two peoples. He reiterated Australia's commitment to the one-China policy, saying that his country is willing to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen practical cooperation in trade, investment, AI and other fields, and deepen cultural and people-to-people exchanges. Australia is ready to work with China on mutual respect and proper handling of differences, so that their relationship can become a model of constructive ties between countries with different systems, he said. Albanese congratulated China on successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' meeting, saying that in the current turbulent world, China serves as an anchor of stability. He also congratulated China on hosting the China-Russia-US summit, which he said is of great importance to global and regional peace and stability. Following his meeting with Xi, Albanese flew to Beijing to attend the 11th China-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting with Premier Li Qiang. During that meeting, Li said China is willing to work with Australia to expand the scale of bilateral trade, optimize its structure, and further enhance trade and investment liberalization and facilitation to achieve more tangible outcomes. A statement on joint outcomes of the meeting was issued on Friday. The two countries agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. This is the third visit to China made by Albanese since he first took office as Australia's prime minister in May 2022. On Friday, Albanese also met in Beijing with Zhao Leji, chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Negotiations for upgraded FTA with Singapore urged
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
President Xi Jinping on Friday called on China and Singapore to launch negotiations for an upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development and artificial intelligence. While meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Xi stressed the need for both sides to strengthen strategic communication, enhance solidarity and coordination, and continuously elevate the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership to new heights. China and Singapore should be sincere friends who trust one another, consolidate political mutual trust, safeguard common interests and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, Xi said. China and Singapore should be development partners leading in innovation, Xi said, urging the two countries to make sustained efforts in advancing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. China and Singapore should be friendly neighbors who learn from each other, deepen exchanges on governance and inter-party cooperation, and expand people-to-people exchanges, he added. Xi called on both countries to serve as progressive forces in upholding international fairness and justice, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks and keep East Asian cooperation on the right track. Wong noted that cooperation between Singapore and China continues to deepen, and the all-round partnership remains robust. Singapore firmly adheres to the one-China policy and opposes "Taiwan independence", he stressed. He said Singapore attaches great importance to its partnership with China and is willing to strengthen exchanges at all levels.

item.title: Talks begin for economic partnership pact with Indonesia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto announced on Friday the start of negotiations to reach a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership agreement. During their meeting, Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on the two countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy and clean energy. He also called for efforts to actively build a blue partnership and reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. China is willing to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation and China-ASEAN, Xi said. Prabowo noted that he and Xi have met four times in recent years to push for significant progress in bilateral relations, and stressed that the strategic partnership between Indonesia and China is stronger than ever before. Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and recognizes Taiwan as a province of the People's Republic of China, Prabowo said. He thanked China for its longstanding support for Indonesia's economic and social development, adding that his country is willing to continuously deepen cooperation with China. He said Indonesia welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business, and vowed to provide a reliable, stable and predictable business environment.

item.title: Xi: Head-of-state diplomacy 'irreplaceable' for China-US ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
President Xi Jinping highlighted on Thursday the "irreplaceable" role of head-of-state diplomacy in guiding relations between China and the United States, urging concrete actions to sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in the relationship. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting. Both sides considered the meeting to be positive and constructive, according to a statement released after the meeting. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive relationship of strategic stability, implement the consensus reached by the two presidents, and build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, the statement said. This was the third meeting between Xi and Trump this year. The two presidents also met in Beijing in May, when Trump made a state visit to China, and in Washington in September, when Xi made a state visit to the US. Xi said that over the past few months, he and Trump have been working together to explore the right path for China and the US, the two major countries, to get along well with each other. The new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity has been well recognized by the peoples of both countries and welcomed by the international community, he said. Xi noted that the overall stability and positive momentum of China-US relations have brought tangible benefits to the people of the two countries, and injected stability and certainty into the world. He expressed his hope to continue working with Trump to jointly steer the giant ship of China-US relations in the right direction toward the future. Xi emphasized that building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented, groundbreaking endeavor that requires an enterprising spirit, hard and solid efforts, and the ability to get things done. To sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in China-US relations, the key is to take concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, he said, adding that communication between the working teams on both sides also needs to keep pace. Xi stressed that it is important to make a longer list of cooperation and a shorter list of problems. Differences that cannot be resolved for the time being should be managed in a constructive way to prevent them from escalating, he said. On the Taiwan question, Xi said the US should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-US relations. He called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns and work toward mutual benefit. Cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. He also underlined the need for China and the US to strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence and ensure that AI always remains under human control. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of US-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. Both sides should maintain the momentum of steady development of bilateral relations, and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence, and fairly address each other's concerns, Trump said. He told Xi that the US does not support "Taiwan independence". Trump congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability. The two presidents also discussed regional and international issues of mutual interest. He Yadong, spokesman for the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, announced on Thursday that the agricultural working group under the China-US Board of Trade will soon hold its first meeting. The two countries' economic and trade teams have maintained communication at various levels, and the two sides held the first meeting of the Board of Trade under the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Nov 13, the spokesman said at a regular news briefing in Beijing. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi calls for inclusive regional co-op based on solidarity, openness, innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
President Xi Jinping outlined economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development as four pillars for building an Asia-Pacific community and opening up new prospects for regional cooperation, as he chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Thursday. The gathering marked the third time that China has hosted the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting, following those held in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. "Today, momentous changes not seen in a century are accelerating across the globe," Xi told the leaders and representatives of APEC economies and heads of international organizations attending the meeting. APEC's 21 member economies are home to more than one-third of the world's population and account for over 60 percent of global GDP. Xi called for efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship, he noted, adding that "to navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other". "We must expand our shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily build a shared sense of community," he said. He called for upholding openness and integration, advancing economic integration and championing free and open trade and investment. Development should benefit everyone, he said, while taking into account the different needs of Asia-Pacific economies. Xi said that China, an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, is ready to work with all parties to strengthen the pillar of economy and trade, upgrade the pillar of connectivity, foster the pillar of innovation and enhance the pillar of development. On trade, Xi said the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific is a shared vision of APEC members, and he called for steady progress in realizing this vision and setting a higher standard for openness. He urged efforts to align regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, reduce barriers to trade and investment, and help economies build the capacity to participate in high-standard economic and trade arrangements. Regarding connectivity, he called for stronger infrastructure networks, closer coordination of policies and regulations, and easier travel for business and tourism. Cultural and people-to-people exchanges should also be promoted to foster mutual understanding, he said. On innovation, Xi described the digital economy and artificial intelligence as engines of innovation-driven growth. "We should build an open ecosystem for innovation, encourage the broad application of AI, and promote the innovation-driven transformation and upgrading of industries," he said. On development, he emphasized the need to promote regional cooperation on energy and food security, deepen anti-corruption governance across borders, and expand green and low-carbon cooperation to achieve sustainable economic growth. He also called for improving livelihoods and investing in people to tap into the full potential of talent across the Asia-Pacific. "China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation," Xi said. He announced that China will provide $20 million to support APEC's practical cooperation, and will establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges. China will also set up cooperation institutions in areas including digital technology, cross-border data flows, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, he said. Leaders and representatives of member economies delivered remarks in turn. All parties spoke highly of the fruitful outcomes of the APEC China Year, thanked China for its excellent work, and made positive responses to the major initiatives and measures put forward by Xi. Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund, who was invited to brief the meeting on the state of the global economy, said that AI has had a material impact on global growth this year, helping counterbalance the economic effects of an energy supply shock. Describing AI as a significant factor in medium-term competitiveness, productivity and growth, she called on economies to develop digital infrastructure, prepare workers for the technology, and address risks to financial stability and cybersecurity. She also underscored the importance of dialogue and cooperation through forums such as APEC, saying that working together can help advance shared prosperity and peace. After listening to the other participants' remarks, Xi called for turning the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into action, maintaining a clear direction for cooperation and delivering solid results to continuously achieve tangible and accessible outcomes. At the conclusion of the meeting, leaders adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which puts forward the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, as well as three outcome documents covering trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnamese President To Lam, whose country will host APEC in 2027, welcomed leaders and representatives to attend next year's meeting. With China's leadership and the positive contributions of its members, APEC 2026 has achieved important accomplishments, adding momentum to economic integration and development in the Asia-Pacific, he said. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn
